title: The Girl From The Farm (Chas McIvor)
style: Afro-folk fingerpicked acoustic guitar warm female vocal storytelling 100bpm Zimbabwe-Australia character portrait brushed drums walking bass honest practical unhurried
lyrics:
[Intro - acoustic guitar, warm fingerpicked, dawn]
She is not someone who needs
A song written about her
Which is exactly why
This song exists

[Verse 1]
She grew up where the distances are real
Not metaphorical distances but actual ones
Where the next farm is an hour if the road is dry
And longer if it rained last week
She helped in the dairy before school
And sometimes instead of school
She knew which cow needed watching
Before the cow knew it herself

[Verse 2]
When the family moved she didn't make a fuss
She made a list instead
Practical in the way that people are practical
When they've always had to be
She found Australia manageable
Which is not a small thing to say
About a country you've never been to
With a man your daughter married

[Chorus]
The girl from the farm
Now the woman with the family
The girl from the farm
Who carried Zimbabwe to Australia
The girl from the farm
Kerri — who came from Jeff and Jill
Who grew up in the red dust certainty
And is still exactly that
Still exactly that

[Bridge - spoken, level]
She didn't come here to be admired.
She came here because Joel was here.
And before that she came from the farm
because that is where her family was.
And the farm came from Jeff and Jill
doing the work before anyone asked them to.
You can trace the line back.
It goes straight.
It always goes straight with this family.

[Chorus reprise]
The girl from the farm
Who knows what she knows
The girl from the farm
Kerri — exactly right

[Outro - guitar alone]
Red dust in Australia
Still on her shoes somehow
The girl from the farm
Is home now
